The blind spot

A lender deposits USDC into a curated vault. One click. A clean APY.

Underneath: an ERC-4626 wrapper, holding shares of another vault, lending into Morpho markets, against collateral that is itself a wrapper of a synthetic backed — four or five layers down — by an off-chain perp desk.

The deposit screen shows none of this. The risk lives in the layers.

20–100×collateral-risk mispricing documented across DeFi lending (Prosperi, 2026)
USD0++ · xUSD · USRthree 2025–26 failures, every signal readable on-chain beforehand

Four illusions at the heart of on-chain lending

Morpho's isolated markets created a false sense of independence. The DIG and YTD reveal a quadruple root of confusion.

1
Independence"Isolated" markets share recursive collateral roots. A wsrUSD depeg propagates up the YTD into siUSD — and into a market with no contractual link to it.
2
TVLThe same dollar counted at every layer of wrapping and re-depositing. Headline TVL suggests depth and diversification that do not exist.
3
DiversificationFive markets, one bet. 85% of collateral can resolve to two BTC custodians — concentration dressed up as a multi-market strategy.
4
(Non-)leverageA passive depositor is silently leveraged by someone else's loop through the same vault. Dark loops — invisible at the deposit surface.

1DIG — the DeFi Integration Graph

The point of view of verbs.

Every token and protocol is a node. Every edge is a relationship — what one thing does to another:

  • wraps — stETH → ETH
  • lends into — vault → Morpho market
  • accepts as collateral — market → token (not a yield path)
  • is backed by — USDe → {USDC, USDT, perps…}
  • cycles into — detected circular reference

The graph is vault-invariant: a token is one node no matter how many vaults touch it. It is the universal map of how DeFi pieces connect.

~400 → 85market references across 20 vaults collapse to 85 unique nodes — 4.75× dedup, ~116 RPC/block instead of ~1200

1DIG in practice — cUSD's neighbourhood

Every wrapper, Pendle PT/YT, lending market and backing edge around cUSD — resolved per block, one node per token.

1DIG in practice — sUSDS, all the way down

Recursion terminates only at native leaves (USDC, ETH, BTC). Depth is the point — each layer is a contract, an issuer, an oracle.

2YTD — Yield Tree Decomposition

The point of view of portfolio decomposition.

Pick one vault as the root. Walk the DIG recursively. Every leaf carries a weight — the share of the vault's assets that ultimately flows through it.

"Your USDC deposit is really 29% wrapped BTC, 33% an off-chain perp desk, 26% a private-credit vault…"

Same machinery, two answers: risk tracing — what backs this deposit — and yield attribution — which leaves earned the APY.

Weights are allocations multiplied recursively along each path — a vault decomposed like a fund.

2YTD example — Sentora PYUSD, $392.7M

senPYUSDmain [V2]  —  $392.7M  ·  net APY 2.37%
└─ senPYUSD [V1]  —  $392.7M (100%)
   ├─ cbBTC/PYUSD     86% LLTV   $113.5M   28.9%   @ 2.31%
   ├─ sUSDe/PYUSD     92% LLTV   $127.8M   32.5%   @ 2.14%
   │   └─ sUSDe → USDe [Ethena]
   │       ├─ Off-chain delta-neutral perps (Copper/Ceffu)  61.6%
   │       ├─ Custodian (USDC/USDT/USDtb)                   30.7%
   │       └─ Custody wallet (wstETH/WBTC/cbBTC…)            5.9%
   ├─ syrupUSDC/PYUSD 92% LLTV   $100.1M   25.5%   @ 2.91%
   ├─ weETH/PYUSD     86% LLTV   $38.9M     9.9%   @ 2.22%
   ├─ sUSDS/PYUSD     94% LLTV   $5.9M      1.5%   @ 3.02%
   │   └─ sUSDS → USDS [Sky] → PSM · Spark · RWA Bloom/Grove · CDPs
   ├─ IDLE/PYUSD       0% LLTV   $6.1M      1.6%
   └─ PT-sUSDE/PYUSD  92% LLTV   $0.26M     0.1%   @ 2.29%
A "PYUSD" deposit decomposes into wrapped BTC, Ethena's delta-neutral perps, a private-credit vault and Sky's RWA stack — none of it visible on the deposit screen.

2What decomposition surfaces that a list hides

Cycles (a token collateralising its own backing vault) · false diversification (many markets, one real exposure) · TVL counted twice along a loop.

3Risk to lenders — the map

Six on-chain-observable factors. Each readable before damage occurs.

Marketpeg / exchange-rate volatility vs. the asset's own history
Counterpartyissuer, custodian, validator — concentration, supply velocity, redemption queues
Smart contractrecursive wrapper depth; high TVL on young, unaudited code
Liquidityexit depth vs. position size; thin PSM buffers
Oraclehardcoded, capped or stale feeds diverging from market price
Governanceadmin mint roles, no timelock, mutable redemption mechanics

3Oracle risk — the price the market sees vs. the price the vault sees

A capped oracle (red) drifts below true market price (blue) — the brown gap is free collateral arbitrage.
Per-block oracle series let staleness and deviation be measured, not assumed.

USD0++ and Resolv/USR both failed here: hardcoded feeds that never repriced while the asset traded at a discount.

3Circularity & leverage — reflexive exposure

wsrUSD/USDT at 94.5% LLTV: borrowers loop debt/equity multipliers toward M max = 17×. The collateral helps back its own borrow market — a cycle the YTD flags and a flat market list cannot.
